reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected SEC exhibit rows shows GAAP earnings and pre-provision revenue lines higher in the later quarter, with a lower credit loss provision and slightly lower total noninterest expense, while company-defined adjusted net income also rose on its own non-GAAP basis. Opposing evidence sits in the credit detail: the allowance balance and allowance-to-loans coverage declined, gross charge-offs increased, and both the reported and the company-defined ex-acquisition annualized net charge-off ratios rose, with the ex-acquisition ratio converging toward the reported ratio. Nonperforming assets and the NPA-to-assets ratio were broadly stable, and the acquired NPA component declined while the non-acquired component was roughly flat. The tax provision increased alongside pretax income, so it is not evidence of a reduced tax burden. The selected rows do not identify drivers: no loan growth, mix, rate, spread, or reserve-build/release reconciliation is included, and the acquisition-date PCD charge-off line has no comparator. Because the extract is a subset of the exhibits and not a complete filing, no conclusion is drawn about items not shown. The thesis remains a source-bounded research record with unchanged conviction; the credit-trend direction and the absence of a driver bridge are the main reasons the view is not upgraded.
